findings: Every factual claim in script.md maps to the spec's closed claim list (C1 to C11), and I found no claim outside it.
Hook: 'designed and built by a software factory called ANVIL' and 'work enters as an intake and leaves as reviewed, approved output' match C1 and C10 and are supported by the source pack.

The line: the intake wording 'a feature, an idea or an issue' matches the pack's safe wording for C2. It does not say 'only' and it adds no other kinds. The spec-before-code, stations-in-a-line and no-self-approval statements match C3 and C4, and 'A human approves before anything ships' matches C6.

The line: 'For software, five reviewers check the work in parallel: spec, security, tests, architecture and design' matches C5. The 'For software' qualifier keeps it from implying these five reviewed this video, which is the caution in the source pack. The video's own panel is facts, voice, brand and design, and it is not mentioned.
Verified memory: provenance tied to a run record, and quarantine for proposals that cannot be verified, match C7 and docs/MEMORY-GATE.md.

Proof: the script leaves out 'first product', which the pack could not source (C10 gap), and uses the safe wording of a concept sensor patch product designed and built end to end. The spoken URL 'sentia dot info dash six nine three dot workers dot dev' matches sentia.info-693.workers.dev. This is the correct handling of the C10 gap, so I am not raising it as a finding.

Close: per-station routing through Cloudflare AI Gateway, the work on GitHub, and Apache 2.0 open source match C8 and C9. 'Wrote, produced and reviewed this video, and it stopped at the human gate' matches C11. It is true by the design of the run, and production-notes.md now exists as the record. The review and gate parts are confirmed only by later stations, so the approver should check them.

Counts: only 'five reviewers' appears, and the script states no other counts (stations, pipelines, panel size). No third-party names, no author name, no employer and no other factory, product or video is named. The script contains no em or en dashes.
Narration length is 189 words, inside the spec's 150 to 200 range. Every section carries a Target timing line.

Minor, not blocking: the script ends at a 1:10 target. I did not check the actual MP4 duration or the production notes, since that is outside the facts scope and belongs to tools/video_checks.py and the other reviewers.
Minor, not blocking: the Hook's 'the product on this page' relies on the hook visual being the Sentia page frame. The storyboard confirms it is assets/sentia-page-hero.png, so the reference holds.
